test_title: Delhi Police Constable (Executive) 2023 - GK/CA (Held on: 02 Dec, 2023 Shift 3)
subject: gk
question:
If NDP at factor cost = ₹1,050 crore

Subsidies = ₹40 crore

Net factor income from abroad = ₹10 crore

How much is NNP at factor cost?
solution:
The correct answer is __**₹1,060 crore**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Net National Product (NNP) at factor cost is calculated by adding Net Factor Income from Abroad (NFIA) to Net Domestic Product (NDP) at factor cost.
 
• In this problem, NDP at factor cost is given as ₹1,050 crore.
 
• Net Factor Income from Abroad (NFIA) is given as ₹10 crore.
 
• Therefore, NNP at factor cost = NDP at factor cost + NFIA = ₹1,050 crore + ₹10 crore = ₹1,060 crore.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Net Domestic Product (NDP)**

 
 
• Net Domestic Product (NDP) is the total value of all goods and services produced within a country in a specific period, minus depreciation.
 
• It is similar to Gross Domestic Product (GDP) but excludes depreciation costs.
 
 
 
• **Net National Product (NNP)**
 
 
• Net National Product (NNP) is the market value of a nation's goods and services minus depreciation.
 
• It includes the total income of a nation's residents and businesses, including any income from abroad.
 
 
 
• **Net Factor Income from Abroad (NFIA)**
 
 
• Net Factor Income from Abroad (NFIA) is the difference between the income residents receive from abroad for factor services (such as labor, capital) and the income paid to foreign residents for their factor services within the domestic economy.
 
• It can be positive or negative depending on whether the nation is a net receiver or payer of factor income.
 
 
 
• **Subsidies**
 
 
• Subsidies are financial aids provided by the government to individuals or businesses to promote economic and social policies.
 
• They are not directly related to the calculation of NNP at factor cost in this question.
